Question: Can we short sell Reliance Industries as we see the movement has saturated?
Answer: Can we short sell Reliance Industries as we see the movement has saturated?: One can short sell any stock including Reliance. Purpose of short selling is to take advantage of the down move and making a profit by buying back at a lower price. One has to short sell the stocks which exhibit some weakness. Weakness manifests itself in two ways: In comparison with the benchmark index. In comparison with its own move over a period of time. Until the weakness is seen, there is no point in short selling. Here is the RELIANCE chart for 1 month: Stock price has moved up from below Rs. 2100 level to Rs. 2233.50 as of today. In the same period, this is NIFTY chart: Nifty index is down to 11211 from 11400 level even after big move over last two days. RELIANCE stock is out performing the benchmark index over last 30 days quite comfortably. In the last 7 days too, the price has not shown any weakness: From Rs. 2211 on Sep 22, it has moved to near Rs. 2233. Conclusion: The stock is not showing any sign of weakness. Hence not a short selling candidate. Readers may have differing views but I go by these very simple guidelines and most of the time the method works. Thanks for reading.

Question: Will all Indian banks go on the way of Yes Bank?
Answer: Will all Indian Banks go the way of Yes Bank? : A good question. Looks like many banks are headed in the same direction. Please read on: But where did Yes Bank go? The sordid details about the bad loans came out, promoters are under interrogation for frauds and at one stage the stock price fell to Rs. 5.65. Fearing a run on the deposits, Government and RBI came up with a quick plan to keep the bank afloat. SBI offered to buy into YESBANK if the share capital was increased and offered to pay Rs. 2.00 per share for the acquisition. JP Morgan revised their target for YES BANK to Rs. 1.00. But the government finally forced SBI to pay Rs. 10.00 per share. Other private sector banks were also forced to invest in YESBANK and HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, KOTAKBANK etc. shelled out their contribution to save YES BANK from sinking. YES BANK is saved temporarily but other banks have thrown good money after bad. It makes no business sense but they had to do government bidding. That is what most banks have been doing ( specially public sector banks) for many years. Banks are not functioning like a business, they are like government offices. The results are hidden for years till finally they are accepted. Liquidity of easy funds from FIIs takes them to sky high prices at some point of time and when that liquidity goes away , the prices crash. Let us look at the top bank in public sector State Bank Of India for its 10 year stock price performance. The stock is a loser over a 10 year period. In the current year it is a big loser. Another one —- Canara Bank: With this kind of performance, it is normal to think that all the bank stocks may go the way of YES BANK. Few days ago, I had answered a question about banking stocks. That answer still remains relevant. Pramod Kumar's answer to Is it a good time to invest in bank stocks for the long term? Are they actually going the Yes Bank way ? : The best way to answer this is to look at the numbers. I am showing the prices of stocks of PSU Banks ( which are part of Nifty PSU Bank Index ) on October 24, 2017 ( the day recapitalization was announced ) , October 25, 2017, and on April 24, 2020 to find out which way they are going. We shall see Yes Bank stock price also over same time period and see what we find. Yes Bank has lost 92% value since October 25, 2017. 7 of the PSU Banks have also lost more than 80% value in spite of recapitalization in 2017 and fresh capitalization and mega mergers in 2019. The biggest of them SBI is down 44.67 in the same period. To conclude : Except for few banks in private sector, all the banks are already on a path similar to Yes Bank. Numbers do not lie. It is our refusal to look at the numbers, our tendency to avoid the bad news which clouds our judgement. Even without the problems faced by Yes Bank, other banks are headed in the same direction. CVID -19 crisis will be one more burden. How that impact will pan out, only time will tell. Signs are not good. Thanks for reading. P.S. : My views are purely based on data and some knowledge about how banks are hiding the bad loans. Readers are welcome to hold different views. Images : Fyers Web

Question: Is Tata Motors a good stock to invest in October 2020 priced at 133?
Answer: Is Tata Motors a good stock to invest in October 2020 priced at Rs. 133?: Yesterday I wrote something in a comment about this stock. 17h ago Tata Motors is one stock which is generally described the way you have stated ( in quotes ). It was traded at Rs. 450 when NIFTY was at 7400 and it trades at Rs. 137 when Nifty is 11900. Little more than 4 years have passed. Same description is still being applied as the stock keeps losing value. I believe my views can be easily inferred from here. People have been talking about this being a good stock ever since the decline from Rs. 450 level began. Market has made multiple all time highs and this stock made multiple new lows. Still it is being touted as a good stock. With every 5–10% up move, there are cheer leaders predicting next higher level. These moves are helpful in getting out at a slightly better price. It is not worth a serious investment consideration. We talk of this being a Tata Group company. We talk about JLR. We talk about new products. As if that matters. Who was managing the company over last 5 years. Same Tata Group which is clueless about the declining sales and market share. JLR has been a part of Tata Motors for quite some time now. Beating around the same bush is not going to get different results. One of their most touted products —- Nano — the small car bombed and took away huge money down the drain. With new models coming to the market from MG, KIA and few others, Tata Motors does not have an actual foothold in any segment in the car market. Trucks are their mainstay. Sales in that sector are a reflection in the economy slowdown. Not much expected from this sector too anytime soon. There is nothing except speculation which can make the prices go higher. Let us learn from the past. Tata Motors 5 year chart: Let us have a look. This decline in price has happened when the market has been on the up move. This is Nifty for same period. While the index has moved up from near 8000 levels to 11930, Tata Motors has moved from Rs. 400 level to Rs. 136. What better signal can we get to avoid this stock? Price tells everything. The record highs in the market could do nothing for the stock price. If another down move happens, we shall be once again be looking at a price below Rs. 100. No, it is not a good stock to invest at any price. These signals are present for last two years and I have written few times about this stock. Question: If the coronavirus lock-down is extended till the 30th of April 2020 in India, what would the poor people do?
Answer: If the coronavirus lock down is extended till the 30th of April 2020 in India, what would the poor people do? : The deadly virus has infected more than a million people worldwide now. Those who are not infected are also affected. The effects are different for different set of people but not good for any of them. Let us see what they would do if the lockdown is extended. Government Efforts : There is tendency among the affluent and the well to do class to put the blame on the Government for everything that goes wrong. The same class also sings praise of the tokenism like clapping or lighting lamps to bolster the mood of the nation. The fact is that these are desperate times. Only the poor people are able to cope up better because they face desperation almost on a daily basis even without the threat of a lock down. Earlier at least they could move out in search of work to earn their daily wages. If they could find work it was alright, otherwise it was desperation. Now it is desperation every moment as even the hope of finding work is taken away by the lockdown. I will talk of Haryana Government efforts to minimize this desperation. Food for the poor : My wife called our maid yesterday to inquire about her well being and to pay some money to tide over the present situation. She replied that she can not move out of her village ( it is a small village in an urban area ) as police are enforcing the lock down strictly and only allowing those people to go out who are working for essential services. She is also working as a cleaner in a bank branch ( banks are essential services ) but has no documents to show for that, hence not allowed to go out. Same story for her husband who works as a cobbler. While they are not being allowed to go out, food is being provided by the government to all the people in this situation. That is one most essential thing which is being taken care by the state government. In case of lock down being extended, I believe this service will be continued. Medicines and Medical Services : Helpline numbers are given and they work. Medicines and hospital services are available and being made available. For all citizens, not exclusively for the poor: Being confined to home is charming maybe for a day or two. Surely not when one of the family members is in hospital and others can not move out to see him/her. I faced this situation myself. My son was at Civil Hospital, Panchkula for 4 days for testing for virus. Other 3 family members were in home quarantine. We were helped by Panchkula Police for sending clothes/ biscuits / toiletries to the hospital. Now the results have come in negative but by way of extra caution we are continuing in home quarantine. Senior Citizens living alone can call the helpline and food/medicine are delivered at home. Police and the health department workers are doing a great job under very testing circumstances. What can we do for the poor? : In my younger days there was a program —- each one teach one. That program spread literacy and education among millions of rural folk who had no access to education. In the present difficult times let us adopt the policy —- each family feed one poor family. Let the government keep on doing the macro management. We can do our little bit without looking towards the government. We can select the families from among our maids, garbage collecting person, dhobi who takes our clothes for ironing, nearby vegetable vendor who is not able to ply his cart and anyone in similar occupations. Or simply contribute to the PM CARE fund. Direct action works fast and better. To Summarize : Sufferings of the poor will increase in case the lock down is extended. Government is doing its best ( sometime less than best ) to alleviate that suffering but it is a mammoth task. Let us not be too critical of the government at this time. ( I am one of the most vocal critics of the government at other times ) We should all chip in with our efforts. Poor people are not poor by choice. Whatever little work opportunities they had, have been taken away by the lock down. Let us tough it out together. Spare a thought ( rather many thoughts ) and some money for the poor. The deadly virus will surely go away one day, our good deeds shall remain with us forever. Thanks for reading. Mother Teresa Quote Image —- Google Images

Question: What will happen when Yes Bank shares are upgraded to LARGECAP on January 5th? Will it have an impact in the price? Since I am holding 43k shares at ₹18, I am little curious about its impact.
Answer: Yes Bank shares upgraded to Large Cap on January 05, 2021? Likely impact?: Not very long ago, Yes Bank was a constituent of NIFTY 50 Index, the benchmark of India stock market. It moved out of that index as the value eroded but remained a part of BANKNIFTY index. It was there among the bluest of the blue chips. It was there as a large cap. Then skeletons started coming out of the cupboards. Price crashed from a high of Rs. 404 in August 2018 to below Rs. 200 by November 2018. People were still hopeful that stock price will turn around and move towards previous high levels. In February 2019, announcement about Ravneet Gill appointment as CEO came and stock price moved from Rs. 187 to Rs. 237 on the same day. Experts on TV channels were ecstatic as if they made a huge fortune. They started talking of Rs. 300 -350 levels within the same month. Nothing of the sort happened. The decline continued. On a fateful day in March 2020, it made a low of Rs. 5.65. That was before the market crashed. Government of India came to rescue through stake sale to SBI and other banks. Management control was given to SBI. Well, market recovered from the lows. Not Yes Bank. Many people are happy to see it at the current price of around Rs. 18.00. These are the people who bought at Rs. 12–13. What about those who had invested in a blue chip large cap stock two years ago? Their tale of woes continues. A picture is better than a thousand words. Does this image inspire any confidence that a big recovery is soon around the corner? To me, it does not. Will being upgraded to a large cap help?: Large caps are not fall proof. It was a large cap earlier. That did not stop it from falling to almost worthless levels. Why only Yes Bank, we have seen other large caps like Reliance Capital, Reliance Infra, India Bulls Housing Finance losing more than 90% of the value in 2 years. Even while NIFTY has recovered and made new highs, these stocks are nearer to their low price than to the high price. Some answers mention that now the institutions will be able to invest in this stock as it becomes a large cap. Why do we forget that institutions like SBI, ICICIBANK, HDFCBANK are already invested in it? What difference does it make? SBI had invested in Kingfisher Airlines and RCOM too. So what? All this talk of stock price likely to move up because of becoming a large cap is clutching at the straws. Stock may go up a few points initially for any reason, mostly speculation but will find its way downward once again. Occasional up moves have happened in the past and we have seen that stock finally went nowhere. Nothing has changed to expect differently. Yes Bank is still a NO. Thanks for reading.
